title: Eight replies can contain fewer useful outcomes than six
situation: In this fictional trial, support manager Nia compares a manual workflow and an assistant on the same ten policy questions. A correct referral counts as a useful outcome.
decision: Use correct answers plus correct referrals as the numerator, with all ten assigned tasks in the denominator. The assistant has three wrong answers; the manual workflow has two.
failure: Wrong conclusion: "The assistant improved performance because it answered 8 questions instead of 6." That counts three wrong assistant answers as successes.
evidence: Check each of the ten task labels against the answer or referral rubric. Assert manualUseful = 8, assistantUseful = 6, and neither wrong answers nor abandonment enter the numerator.
input: Manual: 6 correct answers, 2 correct referrals, 2 wrong answers. Assistant: 8 answers, of which 5 are correct, plus 1 correct referral and 1 abandoned request.
expected: Manual useful outcomes: (6 + 2) / 10 = 80%. Assistant useful outcomes: (5 + 1) / 10 = 60%, despite producing more answers.

title: A second pause must become a referral
situation: In this fictional golden-dataset review, adviser Maya and policy specialist Leila independently label case G-12. Handbook RE-7 says: "One pause per 12 months; maximum 30 days; an adviser must confirm eligibility."
decision: Leila points to the one-pause rule; Maya had treated 30 days as a reusable balance. Applying the stated rubric resolves G-12 to referral-required; save both original labels and that reason with the case.
failure: Wrong draft: "Yes. You used 20 of your 30 days, so you have 10 days left." Wrong dataset action: silently keep Maya’s answer-yes label or erase the disagreement.
evidence: Assert G-12 retains Maya = answer-yes, Leila = referral-required and resolved = referral-required with the one-pause reason. Score the draft for the 12-month limit, four-month fact, RE-7 citation and absence of approval; an answer based only on 20 + 10 = 30 fails.
input: G-12 question: "I used a 20-day pause four months ago. Can I take another 10 days now?" Source: RE-7 as quoted above. Maya labels it answer-yes; Leila labels it referral-required. Rubric: a request outside any policy limit requires referral and must not promise approval.
expected: Resolved label: referral-required. Expected draft: "RE-7 allows one pause per 12 months. Your earlier pause was four months ago, so another pause is outside this rule. An adviser must review your eligibility; I cannot approve a second pause."

title: Split consultation families before changing the prompt
situation: Fictional adviser Jo has consultation notes A1, A2, B1 and C1. A1 is a transcript; A2 is a summary of that same consultation.
decision: A1 and A2 share facts and the expected recommendation. Keeping the whole A family together prevents the held-out result from rewarding exposure to the same consultation.
failure: Wrong claim: "A2 is held out because its filename differs from A1." The text format changed, but the underlying case did not.
evidence: Attach consultation IDs A, A, B and C to the four records. Assert that the intersection of consultation IDs across the two final sets is empty; do not treat the single C case as broad validation.
input: Proposed split: development = [A1, B1]; held-out = [A2, C1]. Jo adjusts the summary prompt after reading A1 and its expected recommendation.
expected: Reject that split. Use development = [A1, A2, B1] and held-out = [C1], then keep C1 unseen during prompt edits.

title: The applicable revision beats the newer draft
situation: Fictional policy owner Leila prepares two Retail Everyday fixtures. RE-7 is marked applicable in the test manifest; RE-8 is explicitly a draft, not a real approved policy.
decision: Filter by the manifest before ranking passages. A later revision number does not override RE-8’s draft state; pin RE-7 and the manifest in the test run.
failure: Wrong draft: "The maximum is 45 days [RE-8]." A genuine quotation from an inapplicable source still gives the wrong policy.
evidence: Assert that returned passage IDs contain RE-7 and exclude RE-8. Rerun with RE-7 authority removed and expect unresolved, not an automatic fallback to the draft.
input: Question: "What is the maximum pause?" RE-7 says "maximum 30 days; adviser must confirm eligibility". RE-8 says "maximum 45 days". Manifest: applicableRevision = RE-7; RE-8 state = draft.
expected: Draft: "The applicable test policy RE-7 permits a maximum of 30 days, subject to adviser eligibility confirmation." The citation identifies RE-7.

title: Missing product means clarify, not an empty success
situation: Fictional adviser Maya selects Retail and types a policy question. The request contract requires both division and product before retrieval.
decision: The missing field prevents source selection. Preserve its absence and return an explicit clarification instead of choosing Everyday as an implicit default.
failure: Wrong response: {"outcome":"draft","answer":""}. The interface cannot distinguish missing scope from a successful answer with no text.
evidence: Submit q-17 without product, then with product = Everyday. Assert the first returns clarify with zero retrieval calls; the second reaches the Everyday source scope.
input: Request: {"requestId":"q-17","division":"Retail","question":"Can I pause for 10 days?"}. The product field is absent.
expected: Response: {"requestId":"q-17","outcome":"clarify","missing":["product"],"message":"Which Retail product: Everyday or Plus?"}. Retrieval calls: 0.

title: A request body cannot grant Business access
situation: Fictional adviser Maya has a server-authenticated session with allowedDivisions = [Retail]. Business Team evidence is restricted in this test.
decision: Use the server session permissions and ignore the body’s access claim. Reject before opening Business evidence, including any cached Business answer.
failure: Wrong result: "Business Team permits 60 days, but you may not have access." The denial arrives after the restricted fact has already leaked.
evidence: Send the forged request with a warm Business cache and again without it. Assert both responses are denied and neither execution reads Business passages nor calls the model.
input: Request: {"division":"Business","product":"Team","question":"What is the pause limit?","allowedDivisions":["Retail","Business"]}. Session permissions still contain only Retail.
expected: Response: {"outcome":"denied","reason":"Division is outside your permitted scope"}. Business retrieval calls: 0; model calls: 0.

title: Recall at two reveals the missing exception
situation: Fictional search engineer Ari labels two passages as relevant to a Retail Everyday question. P1 contains the general pause rule; P2 contains an exclusion.
decision: Inspect passage retrieval before editing the answer prompt. A hit alone hides the missing exclusion, while recall exposes that only half the labelled evidence arrived.
failure: Wrong report: "Retrieval passed: hit@2 is 100%." Wrong draft: "Yes, if you have not paused in 12 months," despite the missing exclusion.
evidence: Intersect [P1, P9] with [P1, P2] and assert one match. Replace P9 with P2 in a controlled run and assert recall@2 becomes 2 / 2 = 100%.
input: Question: "Can an account under review take a pause?" Relevant IDs = [P1, P2]. P1: "One pause per 12 months." P2: "Accounts under review are excluded." Returned top two = [P1, P9]; P9 is an unrelated fee paragraph.
expected: Recall@2 = 1 / 2 = 50%; hit@2 = 1 because at least one relevant passage was found. The exclusion P2 is missing, so the evidence cannot settle this question.

title: A citation cannot turn review into approval
situation: Fictional adviser Jo drafts an answer using clause EX-2. The clause says: "Requests above 30 days may be reviewed by a specialist; review does not guarantee approval."
decision: The source supports possible review, not certain approval. Compare the actual promise with the quoted condition instead of checking only whether a citation exists.
failure: Wrong verdict: "Supported, because EX-2 discusses requests above 30 days." Topic overlap does not support the word "will".
evidence: Mark the claim "will be approved" as unsupported against EX-2. Change only that claim to "may be reviewed" and assert that this narrower claim is supported.
input: Question: "Will a 45-day pause be approved?" Proposed answer: "Your 45-day pause will be approved [EX-2]."
expected: Support verdict: unsupported. Corrected draft: "A specialist may review a 45-day request, but EX-2 does not guarantee approval."

title: Block the synthetic account number before the model call
situation: Fictional adviser Maya uses invented account ID ACCT-4821 in a test request. This teaching fixture treats the pattern ACCT- followed by four digits as an identifier to block.
decision: Stop the raw text at the service boundary and omit it from traces. The adviser can resubmit "Can a Retail Everyday account take a 10-day pause?" without the identifier.
failure: Wrong behavior: the screen displays "ACCT-****" but the model payload or trace still contains ACCT-4821.
evidence: Inspect the captured model-call list and trace bytes for q-18. Assert zero model calls and no ACCT-4821 in traces; test other formats separately because this one pattern does not prove complete detection.
input: Question: "Can ACCT-4821 take a 10-day pause?" Request ID: q-18. The policy tool needs the product and duration, not an account identifier.
expected: Response: {"outcome":"clarify","message":"Remove the account identifier and ask a general policy question."}. Model calls: 0. Trace: {"requestId":"q-18","outcome":"identifier_blocked"}.

title: The second submission returns the first referral
situation: Fictional reviewer system R accepts Maya’s referral, but the caller loses the acknowledgement. The operation key identifies one intended referral.
decision: Persist the key with the operation outcome and compare the payload on reuse. A duplicate delivery repeats the result, while changed content under ref-31 returns a conflict.
failure: Wrong result: retrying creates R-9 and sends a second review task. Another wrong result is silently accepting a new requestId under ref-31.
evidence: Lose the first response after R-8 is saved, then deliver the retry twice. Assert one stored referral and three references to R-8; submit changed content with ref-31 and assert conflict.
input: First submission: key = ref-31, payload = {"requestId":"q-19","reason":"second pause"}. It creates referral R-8. Retry: the same key and identical payload.
expected: The retry returns {"referralId":"R-8","state":"open"}. Exactly one referral exists for ref-31; no R-9 is created.

title: The cancelled Retail answer cannot replace the Business draft
situation: In this fictional test, adviser Maya is permitted to use both divisions. She cancels Retail request q-20 before starting Business request q-21.
decision: Match the returned request ID and revision against the active request before displaying or acting on the result. Arrival order cannot establish which answer is current.
failure: Wrong display: "Everyday policy" under the Business Team selection. A late q-20 approval also must not authorise an action for q-21.
evidence: Deliver responses in the stated order and assert activeRequestId = q-21 and visible draft = "Team policy". Assert no approval or effect is produced for cancelled q-20.
input: Completion order: start q-20 for Retail Everyday; cancel q-20; start q-21 for Business Team; receive q-21 draft "Team policy"; then receive late q-20 draft "Everyday policy".
expected: The interface still shows q-21 and "Team policy". q-20 remains cancelled; its late draft is discarded and cannot request approval.

title: Count useful outcomes within the promised time
situation: Fictional operations manager Nia proposes a teaching target: at least 90% of eligible requests receive a useful answer or referral within five seconds. These numbers are invented, not a production SLO.
decision: Count the referral because it is a useful outcome. Exclude the fast error and the late answer from the numerator, but retain both eligible requests in the denominator.
failure: Wrong report: "90% success, because nine responses were fast." That substitutes response speed for the agreed useful-and-timely outcome.
evidence: Label all ten requests by outcome and duration. Assert eight satisfy both conditions, two do not, and the calculated 80% is below the illustrative 90% target.
input: Ten eligible requests: 7 correct answers within five seconds; 1 correct referral in four seconds; 1 error page in one second; 1 correct answer in eight seconds.
expected: The useful-and-timely rate is (7 + 1) / 10 = 80%. The proposed 90% target is missed, even though nine responses arrived within five seconds.

title: Rollback must remove the withdrawn source from the index and cache
situation: Fictional release lead Sam has release R1 = service S1 + index I7 + policy RE-7. Release R2 = S2 + I8 + RE-8 is withdrawn after a source-authority test fails.
decision: Restore the release set and exclude cache entries from the withdrawn revision. Restoring only S1 would leave both I8 and C8 able to supply the wrong policy.
failure: Wrong result: the deployment reports R1, but the answer still says "45 days [RE-8]" from C8.
evidence: Warm C8 before rollback, execute the restore, then issue the question again. Assert active source RE-7, no RE-8 citation and no reuse of C8; preserve the failed-release record.
input: Current state: S2, I8, RE-8 and cached draft C8 citing RE-8. Rollback target: R1. A fresh question asks: "What is the maximum pause?" RE-7 says 30 days; RE-8 says 45.
expected: Active state becomes S1 + I7 + RE-7. C8 is ineligible for reuse. The next draft cites RE-7 and says 30 days, or returns unavailable until that release set is ready.

title: A stated budget changes the advisory recommendation
situation: Fictional planning adviser Jo compares two workshop venues. Option A costs 400 units and seats 12; option B costs 700 units and seats 20.
decision: Both constraints are explicit, so neither venue is a valid recommendation. Ask about a changed constraint instead of inventing a discount or ignoring three attendees.
failure: Wrong advice: "Choose A because it is cheaper," or "B fits the budget." The first loses three seats; the second ignores 700 > 500.
evidence: Check A: 12 < 15, so capacity fails. Check B: 700 > 500, so budget fails. Raise the budget to 700 in a second case and assert B becomes feasible without changing the attendee count.
input: Request: "Choose a venue for 15 people with a maximum budget of 500 units. Do not split the group." Those are the only available options.
expected: Recommendation: "Neither option meets all requirements. A is within budget but has only 12 seats; B seats 20 but exceeds the budget by 200. Can the budget or venue list change?"

title: Urgency does not change the spending route
situation: Fictional operations lead Nia drafts a purchase rule: up to 1,000 units goes to the team lead; above 1,000 goes to Finance. Only Finance can approve a route exception in this teaching fixture.
decision: Use the 1,200 amount for the route and the authenticated role for exception authority. Urgency can accompany the Finance review, but the requester’s flag grants nothing.
failure: Wrong result: {"route":"team-lead","exceptionApproved":true}. That lets the requesting role approve its own bypass.
evidence: Assert that 1,000 routes to team lead and 1,001 routes to Finance. Submit the 1,200 urgent request and assert Finance routing, exceptionApproved = false and zero purchase effects.
input: Request: {"amount":1200,"reason":"Urgent replacement","requesterRole":"team-lead","approveException":true}. The requester is not Finance.
expected: Response: {"route":"Finance","exceptionApproved":false,"reason":"Amount exceeds 1000; requester cannot approve an exception"}. No purchase is submitted.

title: Keep a policy condition in the same retrievable chunk
situation: Fictional handbook RE-7 has a "Pause duration" heading with a rule and its exception in adjacent sentences. Ari is choosing how to split it for search.
input: Source text: "A pause can last up to 30 days. Accounts under review are excluded." Question: "Can an account under review pause for 10 days?"
expected: Retrieved chunk: "Pause duration — A pause can last up to 30 days. Accounts under review are excluded." Draft: "No under this rule: accounts under review are excluded [RE-7]."
decision: Keep this short rule and exception together under their heading. A chunk containing only the duration sentence cannot answer the eligibility question correctly.
failure: Wrong chunk: "A pause can last up to 30 days." Wrong draft: "Yes, 10 days is within the limit." The split removed the decisive condition.
evidence: Run the stated question and assert the returned text includes both "30 days" and "under review are excluded" with RE-7 provenance. Inspect the chunk text, not only whether RE-7 appeared among the results.

title: Four classifier outcomes produce different precision and recall
situation: Fictional reviewer Leila labels ten synthetic questions as referral-required or routine. The classifier predicts whether a specialist referral is needed.
input: Labels: referral-required = Q1–Q5; routine = Q6–Q10. Predicted referral = Q1, Q2, Q3, Q6. Predicted routine = Q4, Q5, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10.
expected: TP = 3, FP = 1, FN = 2, TN = 4. Precision = 3/4 = 75%; recall = 3/5 = 60%; false-positive rate = 1/5 = 20%.
decision: Q4 and Q5 are missed referrals, while Q6 is an unnecessary referral. Report both errors because precision alone cannot reveal that two required referrals were missed.
failure: Wrong calculation: "Recall is 75%, since three of four predicted referrals were correct." That is precision; recall divides by all five required referrals.
evidence: Compare each predicted label with its reference label. Assert Q4/Q5 form the false-negative set, Q6 forms the false-positive set, and recompute the three fractions from those sets.

title: Remove the permission guard and watch the test reject it
situation: Fictional engineer Ari has a contract test for a Retail-only adviser requesting Business Team. The current implementation denies the request before calling retrieval.
input: Original path: check permission, then retrieve. Mutation: skip the permission check and return the Business passage. Test request: session divisions = [Retail], requested division = Business.
expected: Original test passes with outcome = denied and retrievalCalls = 0. Mutated test fails because the response is a draft and retrievalCalls = 1.
decision: The deliberate defect removes the exact protection the test claims to verify. A test that still passes after this mutation has not demonstrated that it detects cross-scope access.
failure: Weak test: assert HTTP status = 200. Both the denied response and the leaked draft use that status, so the test passes on the mutant.
evidence: Run the original test, apply only the guard-removal mutation, and rerun. Confirm a failure on the denial or zero-call assertion, then restore the guard; a syntax error does not count as detecting the access defect.
